```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yoon_2024_bepotastine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yoon_2024_bepotastine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics16030334>

Yoon et al. pooled a single-dose study in healthy adults with a sparse-sampling
study in children aged 2-6 years to build a population PK model for oral
bepotastine, and used it (alongside a separate PK-Sim PBPK model) to propose
pediatric doses that match the exposure of a 10 mg dose in a 70 kg adult. This
package contains the population PK model only; the PBPK model is a
platform model whose physiology comes from the PK-Sim database and is not
reproducible from the published tables.

# Population

The analysis pooled two prospective studies run at Severance Hospital, Seoul
(Methods 2.1, Table 1):

* **Study 1** -- 32 healthy Korean men, median age 24 (19-37) years, median
  weight 70.8 (56.8-89.6) kg, a single 10 mg bepotastine tablet, 13 samples
  over 24 h.
* **Study 2** -- 30 Korean children with allergic rhinitis or urticaria, median
  age 5 (2-6) years, median weight 17.8 (13-26) kg, 19 boys and 11 girls, given
  1.5 mL of a 2 mg/mL dry syrup (3 mg) twice daily for at least four days, with
  two samples per child (one at 0.5-2 h and one at 6-12 h post-dose).

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yoon_2024_bepotastine"))$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` | log(4.21) 1/h | Table 2, KA; Results 3.1 |
| `lcl` | log(28.0) L/h | Table 2, CL; Results 3.1 |
| `lvc` | log(103.0) L | Table 2, V; Results 3.1 |
| `ltlag` | log(0.27) h | Table 2, ALAG; Results 3.1 |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.75 (fixed) | Table 2, 'Exponent of CL'; Methods 2.2 equation |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1.0 (fixed) | Table 2, 'Exponent of V'; Methods 2.2 equation |
| `etalka` | 0.8198 (CV 112.7%) | Table 2, IIV of KA |
| `etalcl` | 0.04939 (CV 22.5%) | Table 2, IIV of CL |
| `etalvc` | 0.04727 (CV 22.0%) | Table 2, IIV of V |
| `etaltlag` | 0.09982 (CV 32.4%) | Table 2, IIV of ALAG |
| cov(`etalcl`, `etalvc`) | 0.03140 (r = 0.65) | Table 2, CORR of CL-V |
| cov(`etalcl`, `etaltlag`) | 0.03300 (r = 0.47) | Table 2, CORR of CL-ALAG |
| `propSd` | 0.103 | Table 2, proportional error 10.3 |
| `addSd` | sqrt(0.1) = 0.316 ng/mL (fixed) | Table 2, additive error 0.1; Results 3.1 ('additive error variance fixed at 0.1') |
| `cl`, `vc` allometry | `(WT/70)^0.75`, `(WT/70)^1` | Methods 2.2 equations |
| `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)`, `alag(depot)` | one compartment, first-order absorption with lag | Results 3.1 |

# Virtual cohort

The individual data are not public. Two virtual cohorts mirror Table 1: adults
with weight drawn from a normal distribution with mean 70.95 kg and SD 8.04 kg
truncated to the observed 56.8-89.6 kg range, and children with mean 18.90 kg
and SD 3.78 kg truncated to 13-26 kg. Adults receive one 10 mg dose; children
receive 3 mg every 12 h for five days and are observed over the last dosing
interval, the steady-state window in which the pediatric samples were taken.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20240227)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240227)

n_per_arm <- 150

draw_wt <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  wt <- rnorm(n * 3, mean, sd)
  wt <- wt[wt >= lo & wt <= hi]
  wt[seq_len(n)]
}

obs_grid <- c(0.25, 0.33, 0.5, 0.67, 0.75, 1, 1.33, 1.5, 1.67, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24)

adults <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_per_arm),
  WT = draw_wt(n_per_arm, 70.95, 8.04, 56.8, 89.6),
  group = "Healthy adults (10 mg single dose)"
)
children <- tibble(
  id = n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm),
  WT = draw_wt(n_per_arm, 18.90, 3.78, 13, 26),
  group = "Children 2-6 y (3 mg every 12 h)"
)

adult_events <- bind_rows(
  adults |> mutate(time = 0, amt = 10, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::crossing(adults, time = c(0, obs_grid)) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
)

last_dose <- 9 * 12
child_events <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::crossing(children, time = seq(0, last_dose, by = 12)) |>
    mutate(amt = 3, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::crossing(children, time = last_dose + c(0, obs_grid[obs_grid <= 12])) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
)

events <- bind_rows(adult_events, child_events) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Yoon_2024_bepotastine")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("group", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    tad = ifelse(grepl("^Children", group), time - last_dose, time),
    group = factor(group, levels = c(adults$group[1], children$group[1]))
  )
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 4 -- visual predictive check

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 4 of Yoon 2024: 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the
# simulated concentrations (including residual error) by time after dose.
sim |>
  filter(tad >= 0) |>
  group_by(group, tad) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 24), ylim = c(0, 175)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Bepotastine concentration (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Yoon 2024 (median and 90% prediction interval)."
  )
```

The published VPC shows an adult median peak near 75 ng/mL at about 1 h with a
95th percentile near 125 ng/mL, and a pediatric median peak near 70 ng/mL;
the simulated bands sit in the same place.

## Table 3 and Table 6 -- weight-based pediatric doses

The paper's dose search (Methods 2.4) used typical-value simulations: for each
weight, the dose that gives the same Cmax, or the same AUClast, as 10 mg in a
70 kg adult. With linear kinetics that dose is the ratio of the adult exposure
after 10 mg to the child exposure after 1 mg, computed here on a 0.01 h grid
over 24 h after a single dose.

```{r table-3}
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
fine_grid <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.01)

typical_exposure <- function(wt, dose) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose, cmt = "depot") |>
    rxode2::et(fine_grid, cmt = "central")
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, ev, params = data.frame(WT = wt)))
  c(
    cmax = max(s$Cc),
    auclast = sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2)
  )
}

adult_ref <- typical_exposure(70, 10)

dose_for_weight <- function(wt) {
  child <- typical_exposure(wt, 1)
  tibble(
    WT = wt,
    dose_cmax = adult_ref[["cmax"]] / child[["cmax"]],
    dose_auc = adult_ref[["auclast"]] / child[["auclast"]]
  )
}

table3 <- tibble(
  WT = 10:31,
  pub_cmax = c(1.6, 1.7, 1.9, 2.0, 2.1, 2.3, 2.4, 2.6, 2.7, 2.9, 3.0,
               3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.6, 3.7, 3.9, 4.0, 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 4.6),
  pub_auc = c(2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, 3.0, 3.1, 3.3, 3.5, 3.6, 3.8, 3.9,
              4.0, 4.2, 4.3, 4.5, 4.6, 4.8, 4.9, 5.0, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4)
) |>
  left_join(bind_rows(lapply(10:31, dose_for_weight)), by = "WT")

table3 |>
  transmute(
    "Weight (kg)" = WT,
    "Cmax-based, model" = round(dose_cmax, 2),
    "Cmax-based, Table 3" = pub_cmax,
    "AUClast-based, model" = round(dose_auc, 2),
    "AUClast-based, Table 3" = pub_auc
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Recommended doses (mg) by body weight: model vs. Yoon 2024 Table 3.")

# Typical-value calculation: both sides use the same parameters, so the only
# slack is the paper's rounding to 0.1 mg (and its unknown time grid for
# Cmax). Largest observed differences: 0.07 mg (Cmax) and 0.05 mg (AUClast).
stopifnot(
  max(abs(table3$dose_cmax - table3$pub_cmax)) < 0.1,
  max(abs(table3$dose_auc - table3$pub_auc)) < 0.1
)
```

```{r table-6}
table6 <- tibble(
  age = 2:6,
  WT = c(14.0, 14.4, 15.9, 17.9, 19.6),
  pub_auc = c(3.0, 3.0, 3.3, 3.6, 3.8),
  pub_cmax = c(2.1, 2.2, 2.4, 2.7, 3.0)
) |>
  left_join(bind_rows(lapply(c(14.0, 14.4, 15.9, 17.9, 19.6), dose_for_weight)), by = "WT")

table6 |>
  transmute(
    "Age (y)" = age,
    "Median weight (kg)" = WT,
    "AUClast-based, model" = round(dose_auc, 2),
    "AUClast-based, Table 6 PopPK" = pub_auc,
    "Cmax-based, model" = round(dose_cmax, 2),
    "Cmax-based, Table 6 PopPK" = pub_cmax
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PopPK doses (mg) at the median weight of each age group: model vs. Yoon 2024 Table 6.")

stopifnot(
  max(abs(table6$dose_cmax - table6$pub_cmax)) < 0.1,
  max(abs(table6$dose_auc - table6$pub_auc)) < 0.1
)
```

All 54 published popPK doses are reproduced to within 0.1 mg, which is the
precision at which the paper reports them.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), tad >= 0) |>
  transmute(id, time = tad, Cc, group = as.character(group))
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, group) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, group, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, group, time)

dose_df <- sim_nca |>
  distinct(id, group) |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = ifelse(grepl("^Healthy", group), 10, 3))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id)

intervals <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    group = adults$group[1], start = 0, end = 24,
    cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  ),
  data.frame(
    group = children$group[1], start = 0, end = 12,
    cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

## Comparison against published NCA

The paper reports NCA values only for its PBPK model (Results 3.3): Cmax
88.67 ng/mL, AUClast 374.65 h*ng/mL, half-life 2.69 h and Tmax 0.95 h for a
10 mg tablet in adults, described as similar to the values reported in the
literature. They are the closest published reference for the adult arm of the
population PK model, with the caveat that they come from a different model of
the same data.

```{r nca_compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast, ~half.life,
  adults$group[1], 88.67, 0.95, 374.65, 2.69
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "group",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "h*ng/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated popPK NCA (adults, 10 mg) vs. the paper's adult PBPK values. * differs by >20%."
)

adult_nca <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(group == adults$group[1], PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "half.life"))
med_auc <- median(adult_nca$PPORRES[adult_nca$PPTESTCD == "auclast"])
med_hl <- median(adult_nca$PPORRES[adult_nca$PPTESTCD == "half.life"])
# The typical adult AUC is 10 mg / 28 L/h = 357 h*ng/mL and the typical
# half-life 0.693 * 103 / 28 = 2.55 h. A wrong CL, V or unit factor moves the
# cohort medians by far more than 15%.
stopifnot(
  abs(med_auc / 374.65 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(med_hl / 2.69 - 1) < 0.15
)
```

For the children, the PBPK model gave Cmax 75.46 ng/mL, AUClast 350.63
h*ng/mL, half-life 4.08 h and Tmax 1.90 h after 3 mg of dry syrup in the fed
state. The population PK model has no age or formulation effect beyond body
weight, so its typical child at 18.9 kg has CL/F = 28 x (18.9/70)^0.75 = 10.5
L/h (AUC about 286 h*ng/mL for 3 mg) and a half-life near 1.8 h; the paper
discusses this difference between its two models (Discussion), so those PBPK
values are not used as a gate here.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports the inter-individual variability as CV%
  without stating the conversion. The variances use the log-normal relationship
  omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2). The alternative reading (CV% = 100 x omega) gives
  identical values to two significant figures for CL, V and lag time and a
  larger KA variance (1.27 instead of 0.82); simulations under the two readings
  give visually indistinguishable VPC bands for the adult study, so Figure 4
  cannot separate them.
- **Additive residual error.** Table 2 prints 'Additive error 0.1 fixed' and
  Results 3.1 calls it the 'additive error variance fixed at 0.1 ng/mL'. The
  model follows the text and uses SD = sqrt(0.1) = 0.316 ng/mL. With
  concentrations of 1-150 ng/mL the choice has a negligible effect.
- **Proportional residual error.** The Table 2 value 10.3 is read as a CV% (SD
  0.103).
- **Formulation and population.** Adults received tablets and children dry
  syrup; the Discussion notes that formulation and population were aliased in
  their effect on KA, and the final model carries a single KA. The model
  therefore has no formulation covariate.
- **Pediatric regimen.** The children's dosing ('at least four days') is
  simulated as five days of 3 mg every 12 h, with observations over the final
  interval.
- **PBPK model.** The paper's PK-Sim PBPK model is not included; its organ
  volumes, blood flows and partition coefficients are PK-Sim database outputs
  that the paper does not tabulate.
- No correction notice for the article was found on Europe PMC as of
  2026-10-29.
